agenda_text:
This meeting will be held via teleconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-
19 and pursuant to the AB361. All votes taken during this teleconference meeting will be by roll
call vote, and the vote will be publicly reported.

HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may
observe the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. The meeting will be live streamed at
https://malibucity.org/video and https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to
submit email correspondence to bayala@malibucity.org before the meeting begins.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: Members of the public may also speak
during the meeting through the Zoom application. The City requests that you sign up to speak before
the item you would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the
Zoom conference to be recognized.

Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing up to speak
and downloading the Zoom application.

  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

As a result of the Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, the City is under a state of local emergency. In order
to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19, the Commission meeting will be open and public but conducted
virtually because meeting in person would present imminent risks to the health or safety of attendees. This
way, the public, the staff, and the Commission will not be physically in the same place.

The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which are not listed on the
agenda, but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no action may be taken, the Commission
and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items needing response. Each speaker is limited to three (3) minutes.
Members of the public wishing to speak during the meeting must participate through the Zoom application. The City requests
that you sign up to speak before the item you would like to speak on has been called by the Mayor and then you must be
present in the Zoom conference to be recognized. Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions
for signing up to speak and downloading the Zoom application.

Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous meeting where the
public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not subject to public discussion at this
meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final. Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous
meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any
conditions imposed.

Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If discussion is desired, an
item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual consideration. Commissioners may indicate a negative or
abstaining vote on any individual item by so declaring prior to the vote on the motion to adopt the entire Consent
Calendar. Items excluded from the Consent Calendar will be taken up by the Commission following the action on the Consent
Calendar. The Commission first will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been submitted. Public
speakers shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this meeting with no final
action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public comment shall follow the
rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described above are on file in the
office of the Public Works Department, and available upon request by emailing bayala@malibucity.org.

The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device for the deaf (TDD),
please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In compliance with the Americans with
Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please contact Yolanda Bundy, Environmental
Sustainability Director, at (310) 456-2489, ext. 229. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make
reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. [28 CFR 35.102-35.104 ADD Title II].

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury, under the laws of the State of California, that the foregoing agenda was posted in
accordance with the applicable legal requirements. Dated this 19th day of October 2023, at 12:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER

ROLL CALL

ITEM 1.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  None.

ITEM 1.B.  STAFF UPDATES

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated he met with Caltrans, which is preparing
  for a pavement resurfacing project in Malibu from Malibu Creek Bridge to the
  County line. He stated the project design included restriping, upgraded ADA
 Malibu Public Works Commission

  ramps at all intersections, and new traffic loops for cyclists. He stated Caltrans
  had identified potential areas for bike lane improvements, including along
  westbound/northbound Pacific Coast Highway (PCH) from Busch to Guernsey,
  and by Corral Beach. He stated he and Public Works staff would meet with
  Caltrans about those plans.

  Chair Dittrich stated the cyclist loop needed to accommodate low weight bikes.

  Commissioner Major asked if any open items on the PCH Safety Study
  overlapped the new plans.

  In response to Vice Chair Drummond, Public Works Director DuBoux stated
  Caltrans would provide documentation on the existing storm drain lines that
  terminate on Malibu Road.

  Public Works Superintendent Hart discussed the City’s response to Tropical
  Storm Hilary and the Ojai earthquake over the past weekend and Monday. He
  stated the City received approximately three to four inches of rain in a 24-hour
  period. He requested Commissioners report to him any areas they observed that
  needed to be addressed. He stated maintenance crews would be scheduled to work
  over the Labor Day weekend. He stated staff was in contact with Los Angeles
  County Department of Beaches and Harbors about beach entry.

  In response to Vice Chair Drummond, Public Works Superintendent Hart stated
  there was some rock debris on Big Rock over the weekend but everything held up
  well.

  Commissioner Belzberg commended staff for its quick and thorough response.

ITEM 1.C.  COMMISSIONER COMMENTS

  Vice Chair Drummond stated she discussed with Public Works Director DuBoux
  residents clearing weeds at Point Dume Preserve, a National Park Service area.

  Commissioner Major stated there were many similarities between Malibu and
  Lahaina, Hawaii, which was recently devastated by wildfire. He suggested using
  what happened there as teachable moments for Malibu.

  Chair Dittrich agreed with Commissioner Major. He stated Lahaina’s experience
  was also very similar to what happened in the Camp Fire in Northern California.
  He suggested the Commission work with the Public Safety Commission on plans
  for wildfires. In response to Chair Dittrich, Public Works Director DuBoux
  confirmed the siren project would go to the City Council on September 11, 2023.
  Chair Dittrich discussed a large rock that fell on Malibu Canyon Road.

ITEM 3  OLD BUSINESS

  A.  Neighborhood Beautification Program
  Staff recommendation: Provide suggestions to staff regarding elements to be
  included in the Neighborhood Beautification Program for City owned property.

  Public Works Director DuBoux presented the report. He stated he was requesting
  additional input from the Commission on elements and features to be included in
  the program. He discussed potential processes for improvements and
  maintenance.

  E. Barry Haldeman, a member of Malibu Arts Commission and Malibu Film
  Society Board, speaking as a resident, stated he was very much in favor of this
  project. He suggested taking advantage of artists in Malibu. He stated the Arts
  Commission was also exploring public art. He suggested both commissions form
  subcommittees to communicate and coordinate between the commissions.

  Chair Dittrich agreed with Mr. Haldeman’s suggestion.

  In response to Commissioner Major, Public Works Director DuBoux discussed
  the potential process for how a neighborhood-requested project could be part of
  the beautification program. He explained the Commission’s role.

  Commissioner Maclay suggested criteria not be too precise. He asked if the
  Commission was being asked to establish the criteria. Public Works Director
  DuBoux explained the Commission would provide suggested elements. In
  response to Commissioner Maclay, Public Works Director DuBoux stated it
  would not include projects on Pacific Coast Highway (PCH).
 Malibu Public Works Commission
Regular Meeting

  Commissioner Belzberg asked if there was an area staff thought had been done
  well.

  Vice Chair Drummond discussed an application submitted by the Big Rock
  Homeowners Association (HOA) for approximately 3,000 square feet of City-
  owned property that included decomposed granite (DG) walkways. She discussed
  potential funding options. She stated if an art project was added, it would go to
  the Malibu Arts Commission.

  Chair Dittrich asked about legal and insurance requirements.

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated each project would require an
  encroachment permit, which outlined insurance requirements.

  Commissioner Major asked if there were grants available from outside the City.
  Public Works Director DuBoux stated most programs he had seen used city-
  funded grants. Commissioner Major discussed other areas that may not be within
  a specific neighborhood. He suggested that was something the subcommittees
  could work on.

  In response to Commissioner Major, Public Works Director DuBoux reiterated
  that this program was only applicable to the City’s right of way. He stated nothing
  on PCH, a Caltrans right of way, could participate in this program.

  Public Works Director DuBoux summarized suggestions from the Commission
  included landscaping and DG walkways.

  Commissioner Belzberg suggested producing a color-coded map that identified
  areas available to apply. She requested allowable plant materials be identified.

  Public Works Superintendent Hart suggested considering types of items or
  materials that would be allowed, services that would be necessary, and
  understanding of cost responsibility. He suggested including the process for
  dealing with projects that were not maintained as agreed. He suggested
  applications specifically identify who would be responsible for maintenance.

  Chair Dittrich expressed concern with limiting what would be included since an
  applicant may have ideas not previously considered.

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated the Commission should provide
  recommendations for typical project criteria that the Public Works Department to
  use to approve neighborhood beautification projects. These projects would not be
  brought to the Commission for approval. Only those neighborhood beautification
  projects that are seeking City funding would be brought to the Commission for a
 Malibu Public Works Commission
Regular Meeting

Page 5 of 6
_________________________

  recommendation. The Commission’s recommendations would be brought to the
  City Council for final approval on any City funding.

  Commissioner Major asked how the City could take advantage of local artists to
  improve projects submitted.

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated the program was for small beautification
  projects that are within the City’s right-of-way.

  Vice Chair Drummond agreed with Public Works Director DuBoux. She stated
  this program was for smaller, local projects that required only an encroachment
  permit. She added that larger projects applicable for public art would be submitted
  to the Malibu Arts Commission.

  Chair Dittrich suggested commissioners come up with potential criteria and
  submit those to Public Works Director DuBoux who would bring the compiled
  lists back to the Commission for review and approval. He suggested The Malibu
  Times be asked to cover the Big Rock project with before and after photos to
  promote the program.

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated he understood that the Commission wanted
  Council authority to approve grant funding.

  Vice Chair Drummond agreed with Public Works Director DuBoux and suggested
  the grant approval have a limit. She suggested a $10,000 limit for Commission
  approval and no fees.

  Commissioner Maclay and Chair Dittrich disagreed with having a funding limit.

  Commissioner Major agreed there needed to be some limitations to ensure equity
  between neighborhoods.

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated he would provide grant funding options
  when the program was brought back to the Commission.

Subject:  City Hall Solar Project Update

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive an update and presentation on the City Hall Solar
Project.

DISCUSSION: In 2017, the City Hall Solar Power Project was adopted in the City’s budget
and identified as a priority Capital Improvement Project. The objective of the project is to
install a solar power system that will provide City Hall with clean renewable energy that
will not only reduce the City’s overall carbon footprint but also work towards the goal of
making City Hall a Zero Net Energy (ZNE) building.

On June 1, 2017, staff issued a Request for Qualifications/Proposals (RFQ/P) for
engineering design services for the City Hall Solar Power Project. On June 29, 2017, the
City received two (2) proposals, and on July 17, 2017, interviewed the following firms:

  • VCA Green
  • Integral Group

The proposals were reviewed, and the consultants were evaluated by a selection panel
consisting of Professional Civil Engineers, the City Building Official, and the City’s on-call
Solar Energy Consultant. The selection panel identified Integral Group as the most
qualified firm for this project.

  Page 1 of 2
  Agenda Item # 4.B.
 On September 24, 2017, the City Council Authorized the City Manager to execute a
Professional Services Agreement with Integral Group for the Design, Permitting and Bid
Support of the City Hall Solar Power Project.

In 2018, the project design phase was completed and the project was set to advertise for
construction bids. Due to insufficient funding and the impacts of the Woolsey Fire, the City
chose to accommodate other budget priorities resulting from the Woolsey Fire. The City
Hall Solar Power Project was placed on hold through fiscal years 2019-2020, 2020-2021,
2021-2022, and 2022-2023.

The City’s Fiscal Year 2023-2024 adopted budget includes funding for the City Hall Solar
Power Project. The City Hall Solar Project will remain the same in terms of concept and
objectives. The project will include the installation of a solar electrical power system and
EV chargers at City Hall, with project objectives that focus on ways to significantly reduce
the purchased energy and associated operating costs of the City Hall facilities.

The project will have five solar panel carport structures located in the upper parking lot.
These panels are designed to supply sufficient electrical power to City Hall during
everyday operations. Electrical vehicle charging stations are also included in the project.
These charging stations will provide electrical vehicle charging for the public and for future
City vehicles.

Staff will be retaining a qualified consultant to obtain professional services for reviewing
the design plans and making minor modifications as necessary to bring the plans up to
code and ensure the most current technology is being used.
